findings.recommendation: Use the verified GP9/GND pads only after pin orientation is physically confirmed. Test forced recovery in ordinary NORMAL first, remove jumper and prove mask0/profile/schema unchanged. Then do one IO4 mode save/reboot, recover with BT10/GP9, verify forced_recovery and normal CDC, save NORMAL_NKRO, reboot once, and compare full configuration. Abort on missing CDC/identity mismatch; do not retry or reflash.
findings.flash: Device identity/metadata says RP2040 4MiB, but standard RP2040-Zero reference may describe a 2MiB variant; pin recovery does not establish actual Flash capacity. Preserve this distinction.
findings.status: get_usb_mode exposes current/requested_startup/saved_startup/forced_recovery. Normal-mode jumper check should observe forced_recovery=true; after removing jumper, wait for physical_mask=0 and capture full read-only baseline.
findings.mapping: BoardConfig maps source9 to GP9; KeyScanner configures the key GPIO as input with pull-up, and considers low level pressed. Startup samples the source9 down bit before USB personality selection; prepareUsbBoot records forced_recovery and selects NORMAL_NKRO without rewriting the stored mode.
findings.profile_binding: All four preserved profiles bind keyboard source_id9 (BT10/GP9) to HID usage17. Grounding GP9 is also a real key press; a connected host can receive the T key when NORMAL HID enumerates. Keep games, text fields, and other action-sensitive apps unfocused or use an isolated host during both force-normal checks.

limitations: Static source inspection only; no jumper or hardware action by reviewer.
A single forced-recovery result does not verify actual game mappings or guarantee recovery under every electrical condition.
Do not claim board Flash size from firmware metadata alone.
